# Normalized hard-sphere sampling by conserved-currency recursion

29 October 2026. This is an ideal-real/random-source operation for the explicitly
normalized homogeneous three-dimensional hard-sphere equation in GENERATOR.md.
It does not assert a finite-bit continuous output, uniform-in-time work, empirical
gas identification, historical novelty or practical superiority to DSMC.

## 1. Input and theorem

Input is a probability source f0 on R^3 with warranted support |v|<=R, exact known
energy e0=int |v|^2 f0(dv), and an independent source sampler. Fix a>0 and put
h(v)=a+|v|^2, c=a+e0, Lambda(v)=c(|v|+sqrt(a))/a. Source g0=hf0/c must be
sampleable: rejection with envelope a+R^2 supplies it, or an explicit finite
source table can be reweighted. The zero-energy point source may simply be
returned unchanged; no division by e0 is needed if a is otherwise chosen.

For every finite time t>=0, the recursive algorithm below terminates almost
surely, has finite expected total calls and returns a g_t-distributed velocity.
The subsequent a/h rejection returns iid velocities with law f_t, the unique
conservative solution of the actual hard-sphere equation. There is no population
limit, time mesh, weighted output, velocity cutoff or unknown partner-law oracle.
The theorem remains conditional on ideal arithmetic and the stated source.

## 2. Algorithm, including all dummy events

`currency(t)`:

1. Draw v from g0 and set s=0.
2. Draw E of unit exponential law; set s <- s+E/Lambda(v).
3. If s>t, return v. Otherwise call `currency(s)` independently to obtain w.
4. Accept with Q(v,w)=c|v-w|/[h(w)Lambda(v)]. If rejected, keep v. If accepted,
   draw a uniform unit vector sigma, compute elastic p,q, and replace v by p
   with probability h(p)/(h(p)+h(q)), otherwise by q.
5. Return to step 2.

`physical(t)`: independently repeat `currency(t)` and retain the result with
probability a/h(v). The generator identity and physical-law rejection are in
GENERATOR.md. Crucially even rejected collision proposals require the partner
call; its entire cost is counted.

## 3. Pointwise clock drift

The proposal Q is in [0,1]. Either outgoing speed is at most |v|+|w|, so for
the update Vnew (including its rejection and outgoing random choices),

    E_mark[Lambda(Vnew)-Lambda(v)]
       <= (c/a) Q(v,w)|w| <= c/sqrt(a) = K.                 (1)

For the last inequality put x=|v|/sqrt(a), y=|w|/

# Whole review of the normalized hard-sphere receiver

29 October 2026. Root independently read t_velocity_rate/GENERATOR.md and
PROOF.md, plus the actual downloaded Fournier arXiv:1703.10874v1
Sections2.1--2.3 and3. The ideal-real normalized sampling theorem is
accepted at its declared source/model/cost scope.

The outgoing h-proportional choice is essential. Exchange symmetrization
gives the exact transformed generator for g=hf/c, h=a+|v|^2, c=a+e0.
The reverse tests 1/h and v/h recover mass, momentum and the conserved
energy; they do not assume an unknown normalization or evolved sampler.
The recursive executable requests an earlier-time independent partner.
Its pointwise expected clock drift is bounded independently of that
partner's law. The stopped-counter/cemetery argument is a valid adaptation
of Fournier's ordinary termination proof, and pays the whole recursive
tree including rejected proposals. The later fourth-moment estimate
supplies the stated exponential-in-time, rather than double-exponential,
upper qualifier. Neither is a uniform-time complexity claim.

Final a/h rejection gives an actual normalized f_t law with mean cost c/a.
The total-cost identity does not require independence of one attempt's
cost and its success. Bounded observables of independent full outputs
therefore receive ordinary bounded-variable confidence guarantees; no
second moment of an unbounded output mass is assumed.

The actual collision rate is |v-w| with normalized uniform angular law.
This is a real velocity-dependent extension, not a Maxwell closure,
population limit, evolved speed cutoff or Gaussian blur identity.
It still assumes a warranted bounded initial source and known energy,
ideal continuous randomness and exact arithmetic. The actual binary64
execution does not acquire a finite-bit output theorem or physical model
validation. The closest exact weighted construction is ordinary prior,
and the measured finite-population and weighted comparators are faster
at the tested inputs. Practical superiority and historical priority
remain UNKNOWN. The civilisation-level target is not achieved by this
mathematical operation.
